source.prompt: (the vole's) A California vole (Microtus californicus), a wild meadow vole, NOT a mouse, NOT a hamster. One adult on all fours in a neutral side-on pose, feet on the ground, head level. Realistic proportions: 17 cm long including a short 4.5 cm tail, stocky cylindrical body, short legs, blunt rounded face, small beady eyes, small round ears almost hidden in fur. Grizzled cinnamon-brown back with darker ticking, grey belly, grey feet, tail dark above and grey below. No whiskers as strands. No base, no ground. Game-ready.

rig: Template R (rodent), exactly as client/assets/deer_mouse.glb (tools/build_deer_mouse.py) and to be loaded with the deer mouse's constants: BODY 0 (hindquarters), CHEST 7 (pivot at the lumbar), LEG_A 1 (fore pair, elbows) and HEAD 6 (neck, head and the long snout; pivot at the neck) children of the chest, LEG_B 2 (hind pair, stifles), TAIL 3 (lofted, pivot at its root). extras.rig keys (the deer mouse's): kind 'rodent', chest [0, 0.0132, -0.004], tail [0, 0.0078, -0.0269], head [0, 0.0163, 0.0118], fore [0.0038, 0.0034, 0.0073], hind [0.0032, 0.0034, -0.013], length_m 0.11. No TAIL_TIP. No skin.
accuracy_notes: Reads as a shrew, not a mouse: a long pointed snout with a pinkish tip, no visible ears, tiny eyes, a slender low body on short legs, a slim tail; uniform dark brown above, slightly paler grey-brown below, pinkish feet. Still open: the snout is one rigid piece with the head (no separate twitch); the body is the vole's, slimmed, so the shoulders are a little humped; the tail is a thin tube, faintly bicoloured; lod2 (69 triangles) is a dark wedge with a thread tail. Montane and vagrant shrews look alike in the field; the colours are generic Sorex.
